motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, Bailes and McLaughlin reported a single, millisecond-long, highly dispersed radio burst in archival Parkes pulsar-survey data. Its dispersion measure placed it far beyond our Galaxy. This was the first fast radio burst, a new class of cosmic transient that thousands of later detections have confirmed, including localisations to host galaxies and a link to magnetars. FRBs have become a precision tool for fundamental physics. Their dispersion counts the ionised baryons in the intergalactic medium and has resolved the 'missing baryon' problem. They also constrain the Hubble constant, the photon mass, violations of the equivalence principle and compact dark matter. By opening a new observational window, this discovery changed how we probe cosmology and the dark sector, and it now drives programmes on CHIME, ASKAP, MeerKAT and the SKA. It is a landmark of empirical physics.
